topIssues.title: kona-sp1: revm-precompile 42 pulls sha2 0.11, which has no SP1 patch
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Situation

revm-precompile 42 (pulled in by reth v2.5.0, #22495) depends on `sha2 = "0.11"`. The SP1 guest workspace accelerates SHA-256 by patching `sha2` with [sp1-patches/RustCrypto-hashes](https://github.com/sp1-patches/RustCrypto-hashes), and a `[patch.crates-io]` entry only replaces the version it names: the guest patches [`sha2 0.10.9`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2191ce5dd2569534fb3016f7a931eabc78cc6f8c/rust/kona/sp1/programs/Cargo.toml#L137). sp1-patches has no `patch-sha2-0.11.*` tag (only mirrors of the upstream `sha2-v0.11.0-*` tags), and Succinct's own zkevm still pins patched 0.10.9.

So the guest now carries two `sha2` crates: patched 0.10.9 (alloy, kona) and vanilla 0.11.0, whose only dependent is revm-precompile. Two consensus paths hash through the vanilla copy inside the zkVM: the SHA-256 precompile (0x02) and the KZG point-evaluation versioned-hash check. Correctness is unaffected; those hashes run as plain RISC-V cycles instead of the SHA-256 syscalls, i.e. a proving-cost regression. `check-sp1-guest-precompile-patches` caught it.

## Workaround in #22495

revm 42 routes both hashes through its pluggable `Crypto` trait, so kona's `CustomCrypto` now [implements `sha256`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2191ce5dd2569534fb3016f7a931eabc78cc6f8c/rust/kona/sp1/crates/client/src/precompiles/custom.rs#L24) with the client crate's own `sha2`, which is the patched 0.10 line in the guest. The vanilla 0.11 stays compiled in as dead code (`DefaultCrypto`), so the CI check gained an [exemption](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2191ce5dd2569534fb3016f7a931eabc78cc6f8c/rust/justfile#L298-L318): an unpatched `sha2` is tolerated only while revm-precompile is its sole dependent.

Residual risk: the guard checks the dependency graph, not call sites. A future revm-precompile that hashes with `sha2` directly instead of through `Crypto` would regress silently.

## Follow-up

1. **SP1 (Succinct):** publish a `patch-sha2-0.11.0-sp1-6.x` tag in sp1-patches/RustCrypto-hashes. revm-precompile ≥ 42 (revm 42, reth ≥ v2.5.0) requires sha2 0.11, so every SP1 program executing a current revm is affected, not only kona.
2. **Here, once the tag exists:** add `sha2 0.11` to the guest's `[patch.crates-io]`, delete the `CustomCrypto::sha256` override and the check exemption, and restore the strict "every sha2 resolves from sp1-patches" invariant.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topIssues.title: kona-sp1-proposer: resolve foreign ancestors blocking refund claims
topIssues.author: wwared
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Follow up to #22835. A proposer-created game can be blacklisted or retired and therefore eligible to recover its creation bond through refund mode, but resolving that game may still be blocked by an unresolved foreign ancestor.

PR #22835 intentionally does not add permissionless foreign-game resolution. It keeps refund recovery narrow: the proposer resolves and claims only its own disallowed games, and waits when an ancestor has not reached a resolvable state.

## Desired behavior

When an owned disallowed game is blocked by foreign ancestors, identify the minimal unresolved ancestor chain and permissionlessly resolve only ancestors whose on-chain clocks/status make resolution valid. Once the dependency is resolved, continue resolving the owned game and claim its refund-mode credit.

## Constraints

- Do not resolve active or otherwise unready foreign games.
- Preserve parent-before-child transaction ordering across cycles.
- Do not retain foreign games for bond claims or treat them as proposer-owned.
- Keep failures isolated so one foreign dependency does not block unrelated refund claims.
- Avoid a full-history startup scan.

## Acceptance criteria

- A scenario test covers an owned blacklisted/retired game blocked by a resolvable foreign ancestor.
- The foreign ancestor resolves before the owned game.
- The owned game's creation bond is subsequently unlocked and paid through refund mode.
- Unready foreign ancestors produce no resolution transaction.

Filed by an AI coding assistant at the user's request.

topIssues.title: op-interop-filter: Backfill the complete message expiry window
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** I found this during the interop implementation review.

Op-interop-filter's default startup backfill is shorter than its default message expiry window.

Current defaults:

- `backfill-duration = 24h` (`flags/flags.go:49-54`)
- `message-expiry-window = 168h` (`flags/flags.go:55-60`)

Event sequence:

1. Start the filter with fresh storage at timestamp `S`.
2. The ingester starts near `S - 24h` (`logsdb_chain_ingester.go:379-395`).
3. A transaction references a canonical initiating log from `S - 48h`.
4. Message timing accepts the reference because it is younger than seven days.
5. LogsDB cannot find the source block because startup never ingested it.
6. The filter rejects an otherwise valid transaction.

The LogsDB does not prune ingested history. This is a startup backfill problem, not an ongoing retention problem.

The missing range remains relevant for six days after a fresh start. Persistent storage with enough existing history avoids the problem.

Configuration validates both durations independently and enforces no relationship (`filter/config.go:61-68,93-105`).

Expected behavior: default startup backfill must cover the message expiry window. Configuration should reject a shorter backfill window.

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Enforce dependency-set membership during live verification
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** I found this during the interop implementation review.

Op-supernode currently assumes that its managed chains match the dependency set. Live message verification does not enforce that invariant.

`Supernode.New` passes every managed chain to the interop activity. It reads the first available dependency set only to obtain the message expiry window.

`verifyExecutingMessage` checks whether each chain exists in `i.chains` and `i.logsDBs`. It does not call `DependencySet.HasChain` for either chain.

This normally works because operators should manage only expected chains. However, a configuration mismatch can make op-supernode validate messages involving a chain outside the dependency set.

Kona checks dependency-set membership for both the executing chain and the initiating chain.

Expected behavior: retain the dependency set in the interop verifier. Reject messages unless both chain IDs belong to that set.

A startup consistency check may also detect mismatched configuration. The live check should remain the final validity guard.

Relevant code:

- `op-supernode/supernode/supernode.go:83-128`
- `op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/algo.go:158-215`
- `op-core/interop/depset/depset.go:13-22`
- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/interop/src/graph.rs:175-195`

Specification: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/blob/b733da804eeadc597c690f16601091e97af1fc68/specs/interop/messaging.md#messaging-invariants

topPRs.title: kona-sp1-proposer: recover resolution and bonds beyond the observation window
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Games outside the 14-day observation window can still block resolution of tracked descendants. This PR extends resolution and bond recovery to their required ancestors without adding those ancestors to the proposal DAG.

Recovery scope:

- Normal bond recovery continues for games in `state.games`, including resolved entries.
- Only unresolved tracked games initiate parent traversal.
- Unresolved ancestors are followed and resolved parent-first, regardless of age.
- The first resolved ancestor is included for its own credit recovery, then traversal stops—even if older ancestors have outstanding bonds.
- Ancestor candidates are rebuilt each sweep, not retained independently. Recovery can stop before a withdrawal matures if the connecting child or intermediate ancestor resolves, or the child leaves the tracked set.
- No factory-wide historical bond scan, including after restart.

Existing policy and claim safeguards:

- Prestate-based eligibility remains unchanged, including for foreign-created games.
- Defense/proving policy is unchanged.
- Claims respect each game’s own registry, normal/refund distribution rules, finality, and withdrawal delay.
- Paused tracked games retain recovery eligibility; failed claim preflight reads defer submission.

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18429

topPRs.title: kona!: add a chain_id label to every metric, from an ambient scope
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Closes #22529. **Replaces #22569** — same goal, different design. Please close that one in favour of this.

### Why replace it

#22569 threads `chain_id` to the emit: 59 files, ~20 constructors gain a parameter, every `Metrics::zero()` is rewritten, three public constants and `EngineSyncState::apply_update` change shape. It also accumulated 24 review comments, most of them about `zero()` drift that the label work dragged in.

The chain does not have to reach the emit. `metrics::counter!`/`gauge!`/`histogram!` call `Recorder::register_*` on **every** emit, and no kona emit site hoists a `Counter`/`Gauge`/`Histogram` into a field, `static` or `LazyLock` — I checked all ~320. So a wrapping recorder observes 100% of emits and can add the label itself. This is the same shape as op-supernode, which wraps a per-chain `prometheus.Registerer` with `WrapRegistererWith` (`op-node/metrics/metrics.go:160-176`) rather than labelling at each call site.

| | #22569 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| files | 59 | 20 |
| emit sites changed | ~320 | 0 |
| `Metrics::zero()` bodies rewritten | 7 | 0 |
| constructors gaining a parameter | ~20 | 0 |

### Design

New crate `kona-metrics`, ~140 lines of production code:

- `scoped(chain, fut)` / `sync_scoped(chain, f)` bind a chain to the work that emits its metrics, via a `tokio::task_local`.
- `ChainLabelRecorder<R>` wraps the real recorder and reads that binding on each `register_*`.

The scope rides the future, so it survives `.await` and worker-thread migration, but a **new task inherits nothing**. Four places bind a chain, and between them they cover every kona emit:

1. `spawn_and_wait!` (`service/util.rs`) — one line covers all seven per-chain actors. The libp2p swarm is polled inside `NetworkActor::step`, so all gossip metrics are covered here too.
2. `Discv5Driver::start` — its event loop is a detached `tokio::spawn` and it emits the discovery metrics. The struct already held `chain_id`.
3. The jsonrpsee servers, through a `ChainScope` `RpcServiceT` middleware, because jsonrpsee serves each call on its own task. This is the only way to reach the 24 emits in `kona-rpc`. Installed by the node's launcher **and** by the `net` subcommand, which builds its own server.
4. The `net` subcommand's network actor, which it spawns directly rather than through `spawn_and_wait!`.

The remaining emitters own no chain: the `metrics_process` collector on its non-tokio thread, `kona_node_info`, and the start-up zero-fill, which runs on the main thread before the runtime exists. `ChainLabelRecorder::new`'s `fallback` covers those. kona-node serves one chain, so it passes that chain and **every** series is labelled. A multi-chain process passes `None`, so a process-wide emit stays unlabelled rather than claiming a chain it does not have — which also means a missed scope shows up there as a visible unlabelled series, not as a silently wrong one.

The fallback is taken from the **resolved rollup config**, not from `--chain`. `node --l2-config-file` overrides the flag, and the actors scope themselves with the chain from that file, so deriving the fallback from the flag would give a devnet two chain ids in one process: real series under the devnet and a full set of permanently-zero ones under OP Mainnet.

An emit that already carries `chain_id` is passed through untouched, so an explicit label remains available to a component that serves several chains from one task.

### Cost

The per-emit cost is a `task_local` `try_with` — one thread-local read plus a `RefCell` borrow — and, when a chain is known, one `Vec<Label>` allocation plus a key rehash inside `Key::with_extra_labels`. `PrometheusRecorder::register_*` already calls `key.to_retained()` and a sharded lookup per emit, so this is a constant factor on an existing cost rather than a new one, but it is a real one on the derivation hot path. The label value is a shared `Arc<str>` built once per chain, so cloning it is a refcount bump. Caching the extended `Key` per (scope, key) pair would remove the allocation; I left it out because a cache adds a lock and an eviction question for a cost that is not measured to matter.

`kona-metrics` is a hard dependency while the emits it serves are behind each crate's optional `metrics` feature, so the scope is established even when the feature is off. That is one code path instead of `#[cfg]` on a macro body and two spawn sites; the cost with the feature off is an `Option` swap per poll.

### Fit in the lokahi stack

#22599 ("lokahi: run N chains in one process") merged #22569's threading into its composition line and adds `Metrics::init(chain_id)` per chain plus ~26 `Arc<str>` label fields. Against this PR it needs none of that. What it needs instead is small and already has the seam: it composes each chain then flattens every chain's actors into one `run_actors` call, and `label_chain`/`ChainLabeledActor` already carries the chain id across that boundary — so `ChainLabeledActor::step_erased` wraps its inner step in `kona_metrics::scoped`, `init_prometheus_server` is called with `None`, and each chain's `Metrics::init` runs in a `sync_scoped`. Its multi-chain `L1WatcherActor` — the one component that serves N chains from a single task, and the case ambient scoping genuinely cannot handle — emits no metrics at all, so it needs nothing.

### Verification

**End to end, on the real binary.** kona-node built and run with `--metrics.enabled -c 11155420`, then `/metrics` scraped: **168 series, every one carrying `chain_id="11155420"`, none without.** That includes `process_cpu_seconds_total`, `kona_node_info`, `kona_node_rollup_config`, and the whole zero-fill — with zero emit-site changes.

**The config-file path too.** Run with `-c 10` but `--l2-config-file` naming chain `424242`: all 168 series carry `chain_id="424242"`. Before that fix they would have carried `10`.

**Both spawn seams are regression-tested, not asserted.**

- `actor_metrics_carry_the_chain_the_supervisor_was_given` drives `spawn_and_wait!` with a stub `NodeActor` that awaits and then emits. Remove the scope from the macro and it fails with `left: [None]`.
- `rpc_handler_metrics_carry_the_launcher_chain` launches a real jsonrpsee server through `JsonrpseeServerLauncher`, calls a method over HTTP, and asserts the label. Point the middleware at a different chain and it fails with `left: [Some("0")]`.

Both need the process-global recorder, since a thread-local one cannot reach a spawned task; `test_metrics.rs` owns the single install.

**7 tests in `kona-metrics`** cover the recorder and the scope semantics, including `a_spawned_task_does_not_inherit_the_scope`, which pins the limitation the design is built around so a change in tokio's behaviour is caught here rather than by a mislabelled dashboard.

244 tests pass across kona-metrics, kona-cli, kona-disc, kona-node-service, kona-node and kona-rpc. `clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings` clean. `cargo check` with default features clean for each package individually, not just in the workspace. `lint-docs` reproduced locally with CI's exact `RUSTDOCFLAGS` on the pinned nightly.

### Not in scope

- `kona_node_engine_task_failure`'s dynamic label key is fixed in #22705, and the `Metrics::zero()` drift in #22706. Both were found by #22569; neither needs the chain work, and splitting them keeps all three reviewable.
- `kona-metrics` is not wired into kona-host or the sp1 host. Neither is multi-chain, and the sp1 host installs its own recorder.
- jsonrpsee runs a subscription callback under `tokio::spawn` and a blocking method under `spawn_blocking`, so neither inherits the middleware's scope. kona registers four subscriptions and no blocking method, and none of the four emits a metric; the limitation is documented on `ChainScope`.
- Nothing forces a new spawn site to be scoped. The `None` fallback makes an unscoped emit visible in a multi-chain process rather than wrong, which is the cheap version; a lint or an assertion in lokahi's acceptance run would be the thorough one.

BREAKING CHANGE: three public items of `kona-cli` change, so it goes to 0.4.0. `MetricsArgs::init_metrics` and `init_prometheus_server` take a `chain_id: Option<u64>`, `init_prometheus_server` returns `CliResult` rather than `Result<(), BuildError>`, and `CliError` gains two variants. `CliError` is `#[non_exhaustive]` now, so later variants are additive. No in-repo caller outside `bin/node` is affected.

topPRs.title: kona-engine: record the L1 origin of the local-safe head
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Part of #22528. Groundwork for the atomic snapshot query in #22527.

### Before

The engine's sync state held a local-safe head with no record of which L1 block it was derived from. To answer "which L1 block was the chain safe at, at this L2 timestamp?" — the query interop uses to decide cross-safety — a caller had to pair the head with a `derived_from` observed somewhere else, and the ChainController cannot do that reliably:

- The engine task queue is a `BinaryHeap` (`task_queue/core.rs`) and `EngineTask::Ord` returns `Ordering::Equal` for two `Consolidate` tasks, so among equal-priority consolidations the last `derived_from` forwarded is not guaranteed to be the last one executed.
- `Engine::drain` peeks, executes, and only then pops, so a task error halts the drain with that task still queued. A drain can end with local-safe written by an earlier task while later-forwarded origins were never consumed — pairing would then report an L1 key *ahead of* the head. `ChainController::step` drains at the top and enqueues at the bottom, so more than one consolidation really can be in flight.
- Two writers hold no L1 key at all: the derivation-delegation path, where the input is a bare `L2BlockInfo`, and engine resets, which install a walkback point found by traversing L2.

A wrong L1 key here is worse than no answer, since the caller has no way to tell the two apart.

### After

The pairing is recorded by the writer of the head, in the same step that writes it, and read back through one call:

- `EngineSyncState::local_safe()` returns the head and its origin from a single snapshot, so a consumer cannot observe a head from one update beside an origin from another. That is the read path #22527's handler needs; the handler itself is not in this PR.
- No writer can move the local-safe head without saying where it came from — the origin is part of the update, not a field beside it.
- Writers with no L1 key record an explicit "unpaired" rather than leaving a stale origin behind. A reset thereby *invalidates* the pairing it supersedes, instead of leaving one that describes a head the engine is no longer on.
- The absent case is a distinct variant, so a consumer cannot mistake it for a real L1 block the way a flattened `Option<BlockInfo>` defaulted to block 0 could.

### How

`LocalSafeOrigin` is `Unpaired | DerivedFrom(BlockInfo)`. `LocalSafeHead` bundles a head with its origin and is both the write shape — `EngineSyncStateUpdate::local_safe_head` becomes an `Option<LocalSafeHead>` — and the read shape.

`ConsolidateInput` derives the origin from its own variant: attributes supply their `derived_from`, a delegated `L2BlockInfo` is unpaired. `Engine::reset` / `reset_to` write unpaired. `InsertTask` trades `is_payload_local_safe: bool` for `local_safe_origin: Option<LocalSafeOrigin>`, carrying the same "is this local-safe at all" bit in its outer layer and the L1 key in its inner one; `SealTask` supplies it from the attributes it already holds, so nothing new is threaded through the build path. The Holocene deposits-only retry keeps the origin for free, since `as_deposits_only` copies `derived_from`.

Not in scope: #22528's rocksdb SafeDB store and #22527's query handler. Both issues stay open.


---

topPRs.title: kona-node-service: EngineActor becomes ChainController
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Part of #22527. Stacked on #22586.

**Before.** The actor that owns a chain's head state was called `EngineActor`, as if it wrapped the Engine API. Under interop a multi-chain host runs one of these per chain, so the name reads as one engine per chain. Separately, a gossiped payload at or below the local-safe head was inserted anyway, rewinding the unsafe head under a head derived from L1 and breaking `unsafe >= local-safe`.

**After.** It is the `ChainController`: the sole writer of the engine's heads, the mediator of every derivation-bound signal, and the owner of reset initiation. A gossiped payload is now admitted only if it descends from the local-safe head.

**How.** The rename covers the types that named the actor rather than the Engine API — `EngineActorRequest`, `EngineError`, `EngineRpcActor`/`EngineRpcRequest`, `EngineDerivationClient`, `EngineClientError`/`EngineClientResult`, and the `actors::engine` module. The last two also resolve a collision with kona-engine's own `EngineClientError`. `EngineConfig` keeps its name (it configures the real Engine API connection), as do the per-consumer `DerivationEngineClient` / `NetworkEngineClient` / `SequencerEngineClient` traits, which are named for their consumer. No wire names change: RPC methods, WS subscriptions and `dev_subscribe_engine_queue_size` are untouched, and the `engine` tracing target stays so operator log filters keep working.

The payload check rejects the two cases decidable from state on hand — a payload at or below the local-safe head, and one exactly above it whose parent is not that head — and admits anything further ahead, whose ancestry is not available and which derivation settles when local-safe catches up. Untrusted input is rejected rather than clamped: the payload is dropped at the queue boundary, next to the existing drop for an `INVALID` payload status. The check reads the state the write itself uses rather than the state at enqueue time, which the local-safe head can outrun; `EngineSyncState::apply_update` deliberately clamps only the cross-safe head, and this is what makes its assumption that no writer produces an unsafe head below it true for the one writer fed from outside the node.

**Not in this PR.** The issue also asks for a read-only query handler serving an atomic local-safe-at-timestamp plus L1-at-safe snapshot. That needs the L2 head paired with the L1 block it was derived from, and the pairing has to be recorded where the local-safe head is written, not inferred afterwards by the controller — a consolidation can fall back to build-and-seal and land a different block than the attributes named, so pairing "last `derived_from` forwarded" with "local-safe head after drain" can silently answer with an L1 key the head was not derived from. That makes it a `kona-engine` sync-state change, and it wants its own slice. Left as a follow-up on #22527; details in a comment there.

Two other items on the issue already hold from earlier slices in this stack and are unchanged here: the controller already mediates the derivation-bound signals and owns reset initiation, and the depth-1 lockstep confirmation is already fed from local-safe (with a lagging-cross test asserting it).

topPRs.title: kona: make the pre-created metric series match what the code emits
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
`Metrics::zero()` pre-creates one series per expected label tuple so Prometheus exposes it before the first event. Nothing links that list to the emit sites, and the two had drifted apart in both directions. A series no code can produce sits at 0 forever beside the real ones, and an emitted series is missing until its first event — which is the gap `zero()` exists to close. Three shipped dashboard panels are empty today because of it.

Every label list is now derived from the emit sites, and written as a loop over the emitted values rather than one call per series.

### Corrected in `zero()`

|metric|was|is|
|---|---|---|
|`kona_node_dial_peer_error`|one unlabelled series|the 9 `type` values emitted by `driver.rs`/`gater.rs`|
|`kona_node_find_node_requests`|one unlabelled series|the constant `find_node` label the emit carries|
|`kona_node_rpc_calls`|17 methods|19 — adds the emitted `opp2p_unblockPeer` and `admin_postUnsafePayload`|
|`kona_node_block_validation_failed`|12 reasons|11 — drops `parent_beacon_root`, which no `BlockInvalidError` variant produces|
|`kona_node_gossip_events`|5 `type` values|the 2 topic-free ones|
|`kona_node_banned_peers`|one unlabelled series|not pre-created|
|`kona_providers_chain_rpc_calls` / `_errors`|4 methods|5 — adds the emitted `block_by_number`|
|`kona_providers_beacon_requests` / `_errors`|`blob_sidecars`|`blobs`, which is what `beacon_client.rs` emits|
|`kona_providers_l2_chain_requests` / `_errors`|3 methods, 2 with no code path|the 2 emitted: `l2_block_by_hash`, `l2_block_ref_by_number`|
|`kona_providers_local_cache_hits` / `_misses`|included `block_by_hash`, omitted `l2_block_info_by_hash`|the 4 methods `buffered.rs` emits|

Two of these need a word on why the fix goes the way it does. `kona_node_gossip_events` pre-created five `type` values, but the `message`, `subscribed` and `unsubscribed` emits also carry `topic`; for the last two the topic is whatever a remote peer announces, so the value set is not knowable at startup. `kona_node_banned_peers` carries `peer_id` and `score`, so it has no finite series set either. Both keep their emits and drop the phantom pre-created series.

`opp2p_peerStats` was pre-created, but `P2pRpc::opp2p_peer_stats` was the one handler of eighteen with no emit at all. That reads as the omission, so the emit is added rather than the series removed.

`SEQUENCER_STATE` was declared with `describe_counter!` and is emitted with `metrics::gauge!`, so the description never attached to the series. Same class of defect, one line.

### Removed

Four metrics were declared and described but emitted by nothing anywhere in `rust/`. They are removed rather than left reporting a permanent 0: `kona_node_gossipsub_events` (duplicated `kona_node_gossip_events`, which carries the real data), `kona_providers_cache_memory_bytes`, `kona_providers_request_duration` and `kona_providers_local_cache_capacity`.

Only `kona_providers_cache_memory_bytes` had a consumer: the "Cache Memory Usage" panel on both kona-node dashboards, rendering the constant 0 from `zero()`. That panel is removed with it. The other three had none.

While checking consumers I found the dashboards querying two metric names that do not exist — `kona_providers_blob_sidecar_fetches` and `kona_providers_blob_sidecar_errors`, against emitted names `kona_providers_blob_fetches` and `kona_providers_blob_fetch_errors`. Same drift, other direction; those two panels now use the emitted names.

### Verification

13 new tests render `zero()` through a `DebuggingRecorder` and assert the pre-created label set for each corrected metric. All fail on `develop`. `cargo test --all-features` across kona-gossip, kona-disc, kona-providers-alloy, kona-providers-local, kona-derive, kona-node-service and kona-rpc passes, except `kona-disc driver::tests::test_online_discv5_driver_bootstrap_testnet`, which dials real testnet boot nodes and fails identically on `develop`. `clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings` clean over those crates plus kona-node. `cargo build -p kona-derive --target riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf --no-default-features` still builds.

### Deliberately not in scope

These are real defects found on the way. They are behavioural changes or separate work, so they are recorded here rather than folded in.

- Metrics with no `zero()` entry at all: 17 in kona-derive, 6 in kona-node-service. That is the pre-existing scope of `zero()`, not drift. Several are level gauges where publishing a fake 0 height is arguably worse than an absent series, so it needs a decision rather than a sweep.
- `kona_node_banned_peers` uses `inc!(gauge, ..)` per `peer_id`, so it is a one-shot 1 per peer rather than a count, and its cardinality is unbounded.
- `kona_derive_batch_validity` carries 26 free-text `BatchDropReason` sentences as label values.
- `kona_providers_cache_entries` uses `inc!` on insert against a bounded `LruCache`, so it grows without bound and never reflects the real entry count.
- `SEQUENCER_STATE` sets the current `active`/`recovery` combination to 1 and never clears the previous one, so two series read 1 after any flip.
- `RollupRpc::RPC_IDENT` is `"rollup_rpc"`: off-convention name, never described, never zeroed.
- Nothing prevents this drifting again. The structural fix is to make the label values constants that both the emit and `zero()` read, or to add a lint. `kona_node_engine_task_failure` in #22705 shows the shape, using `EngineTaskErrorSeverity::ALL`.

Split out of #22569, which found most of this while adding a chain dimension. It is independent of that work, and much easier to review on its own.
